section: Section 2 -> Learning Outcomes table -> row 'CLO2'; Section 3 -> Assessment table -> row 'Midterm Exam (closed book)'
summary: CLO2 is stated at Create level but is mapped only to the exam-only Midterm Exam component, with no project/design/critique deliverable mapped to it.
suggested_fix: Add CLO2 to the CLO-Mapped column of the Project row (or another project/design/critique component) so a stated Create-level outcome is assessed by more than a closed-book exam.

summary: CLO2's verb 'Define' is a literal Bloom's Remember-level verb, but the CLO states Create -- a 5-level over-claim mismatch.
suggested_fix: Either reword CLO2 with a verb that genuinely supports Create-level demand and map it to a project/design deliverable, or correct the stated Bloom level to match the verb (e.g. Remember) and confirm the exam-based assessment mapping is adequate at that corrected level.

summary: CLO2 -> PLO3 is a valid PLO ID but a poor pedagogical fit: a pure recall outcome mapped to a design-outcome PLO; PLO1 would fit better.
suggested_fix: Consider remapping CLO2 to PLO1 unless the course intends CLO2 to culminate in an actual design task, in which case verb, Bloom level, and assessment mapping should all be revised together.

summary: CLO1 does not map to any PLO ID; the PLO column contains a placeholder dash ('-') instead of a PLO code.
suggested_fix: Add at least one PLO code (e.g. PLO1) to the PLO column of the CLO1 row, referencing references/plo-catalog.md.

summary: CLO1 has no PLO mapping and no stated justification for the omission; per plo-catalog.md's validity rule and tabee-standard.md this is a missing-mapping defect, leaving CLO1's teamwork/foundational content uncounted toward any PLO (e.g. PLO9, PLO1) while only PLO2/PLO3 are currently verifiable for this course.
suggested_fix: Add at least one valid PLO code from plo-catalog.md to CLO1's PLO column (PLO9 or PLO1 are plausible fits), or add an explicit stated justification per plo-catalog.md's validity rule if intentionally left unmapped.

summary: CLO2 is stated as Analyze but its verb chain ('analyze'/'critique') classifies as Evaluate, one level above stated -- an under-claim of cognitive demand.
suggested_fix: Either raise the stated Bloom level to Evaluate to match the 'critique' verb, or reword to drop 'critique' if Analyze is the intended ceiling (e.g. 'analyze and compare the design of games made by others and by oneself').

summary: CLO2's effective Evaluate level (per F003) is mapped only to the 'Individual' assessment component (29.5%), which has no documented rubric/method distinguishing it as a critique/peer-review deliverable -- insufficient evidence of congruence.
suggested_fix: Clarify in Section 3 (or the rubric) what the 'Individual' component consists of, e.g. rename it 'Individual design critique report', or add a distinct critique-type component and map CLO2 to it.
